description:
Coverage plan — no implementation performed. Edit test/zaq/engine/connect/device_protocol_test.exs; retain its async: true unit-test setup and existing @credential fixture. Exercise only Codex’s public functions with literal response maps and fake device identifiers. No database, HTTP, Mox, application configuration, secrets, processes, or timers are needed.

Missed line 36: Call Codex.initiate_response(500, valid_body) and Codex.initiate_response(200, nil); each returns {:error, :oauth_failed}. This distinguishes unsuccessful HTTP status and non-map response from a valid initiation.
49: Call Codex.poll_response(400, %{"error" => "authorization_pending"}, 7); assert {:pending, 7}. The provider error, rather than HTTP status, controls this result. Optionally repeat with status 200 to protect that precedence.
56: Call Codex.poll_response(403, nil, 7) and (404, "not-json", 7); assert {:pending, 7} for both. These exercise non-map responses, whereas existing 403/404 tests use maps.
57: Call Codex.poll_response(200, nil, 7) and (500, [], 7); assert {:terminal, :failed}. This separates malformed successful and unsuccessful responses from the pending-status exception.
88: Supply otherwise valid initiation material with "interval" => "7seconds"; assert {:error, :oauth_failed}. Repeat with "" if useful: a partially parsed or empty interval must not schedule polling.
92: Supply otherwise valid initiation material with "interval" => nil and 7.5; assert {:error, :oauth_failed} for each non-string/non-integer value.

Add boundary examples alongside these gaps: absent "interval" yields the documented five-second default; explicit 1 and 900 succeed, while 0 and 901 fail. Assert the fixed expires_in: 900, verification URL, and exact two-key material on success, rather than only a broad {:ok, _} shape. Reuse the existing property-test setup to extend the current nonpositive-integer property to out-of-range positive integers (e.g. 901..10_000), asserting none produce scheduling instructions. Keep concrete malformed-string and nonnumeric examples: the property must not replace them.

These are pure protocol tests, so they need no synchronization or global-state restoration. During implementation, run the isolated test file and inspect fresh line coverage; do not weaken its existing assertions. The relevant device-protocol Beadwork issue (zaq-p8t.1) is closed; no matching open planning issue was found.

Coordinator validation override: no coverage runs by workers; final targeted coverage is centrally run after mix q. Action reuse N/A test-only. Independent root step; no dependencies.
title: zaq-p8t.8.1 Add Codex device protocol boundary coverage
